value.zh: 楊終字子山，蜀郡成都人也。
value.en: Yang Zhong, styled Zishan, came from Chengdu in Shu commandery.
value.literal: Yang Zhong, courtesy name Zishan, was a man of Chengdu in Shu commandery.

value.zh: 年十三，為郡小吏，太守奇其才，遣詣京師受業，習春秋。
value.en: When he was thirteen he served as a junior clerk in the commandery. The grand administrator, struck by his ability, sent him to the capital for schooling, and there he mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals.
value.literal: At age thirteen he became a petty clerk in the commandery; the grand administrator marveled at his talent and sent him to the capital to study, where he learned the Chunqiu.

value.zh: [一]顯宗時，征詣蘭台，拜校書郎。
value.en: Under Emperor Ming he was called to the Orchid Terrace and given the post of collating secretary [1].
value.literal: In the time of Emperor Ming [note 1], he was summoned to the Orchid Terrace and appointed collator.

value.zh: 初，酺之為大匠，上言：「孝文皇帝始置一經博士，[一]武帝大合天下之書，[二] 而孝宣論六經於石渠，學者滋盛，弟子萬數。
value.en: Earlier, when Pu was superintendent of construction, he submitted a statement: 'Emperor Wen first established erudites for a single classic; [1] Emperor Wu broadly gathered the books of All under Heaven; [2] while Emperor Xuan debated the six classics at the Stone Canal—scholars flourished and disciples numbered in the tens of thousands.
value.literal: Earlier, when Pu was superintendent of construction, he submitted a statement: 'Emperor Wen first established erudites for a single classic; [1] Emperor Wu broadly gathered the books of All under Heaven; [2] while Emperor Xuan debated the six classics at the Stone Canal—scholars flourished and disciples numbered in the tens of thousands.

value.zh: [三]光武初興，愍其荒廢，起太學博士捨、內外講堂，諸生橫巷，為海內所集。
value.en: [3] Emperor Guangwu, grieving the ruin of learning, had rebuilt the Grand Academy with dormitories, inner and outer lecture halls, and student quarters that drew scholars from everywhere.
value.literal: [3] When Guangwu first rose, pitying their ruin and waste, he raised the Grand Academy, erudite lodgings, inner and outer lecture halls, and lanes of students—it became the gathering place of the realm.

value.zh: 明帝時辟雍始成，欲毀太學，太尉趙憙以為太學、辟雍皆宜兼存，故並傳至今。
value.en: When Emperor Ming finished the circular moat school, some wanted the Grand Academy torn down; Grand Commandant Zhao Xi argued that both institutions should survive, and both stand today.
value.literal: In Emperor Ming's time, when the Biyong was first completed, they wished to destroy the Grand Academy. Grand Commandant Zhao Xi held that the Grand Academy and the Biyong should both be kept, and therefore both have been transmitted to the present.

value.zh: 而頃者頹廢，至為園采芻牧之處。
value.en: Lately the grounds had fallen into disuse as vegetable patches, hayfields, and sheep walks.
value.literal: But recently it has decayed and wasted until it became a place for garden plots, gathering fodder, and herding.

value.zh: 宜更修繕，誘進後學。」
value.en: Zhai Pu urged a fresh restoration to attract the next generation of learners."
value.literal: It is fitting to repair and build anew and entice later students.'

value.zh: 帝從之。
value.en: The emperor accepted the advice.
value.literal: The emperor followed it.'"

value.zh: 酺免後，遂起太學，更開拓房室，學者為酺立碑銘於學雲。
value.en: After his disgrace the Grand Academy was rebuilt and expanded; students are said to have raised a stele in his honor on the campus.
value.literal: After Pu was dismissed, thereupon they raised the Grand Academy, again opened and expanded rooms, and scholars set up a stele inscription for Pu at the academy, it is said.

value.zh: 注[三]宣帝甘露三年，詔諸儒講五經於殿中，兼平公羊、谷梁同異，上親臨決焉。
value.en: Commentary [3]: In Ganlu 3 Emperor Xuan held a palace conference on the five classics and adjudicated Gongyang versus Guliang in person.
value.literal: Note [3] In Emperor Xuan's Ganlu 3 an edict ordered the scholars to lecture on the five classics in the palace, also settling agreements and differences between Gongyang and Guliang, and the emperor personally attended to decide.

value.zh: 時更崇谷梁傳，故此言「六經」也。
value.en: At that time they further honored the Guliang commentary, hence this speaks of 'six classics.'
value.literal: At that time they further honored the Guliang commentary, hence this speaks of 'six classics.'

value.zh: 石渠，閣名。
value.en: Stone Canal was the name of the palace gallery where the debate met.
value.literal: Stone Canal is the name of a pavilion.

value.zh: 昭帝時博士弟子員百人，宣帝末增倍之，元帝時詔無置弟子員，以廣學者，故言以萬數也。
value.en: Student rolls had grown from one hundred under Zhao to doubled under Xuan, then Yuan removed caps so enrollments could soar toward ten thousand.
value.literal: In Emperor Zhao's time erudite disciples numbered one hundred; at the end of Emperor Xuan it was doubled; in Emperor Yuan's time an edict ordered not to fix a quota of disciples so as to broaden learners—hence it says they numbered in the tens of thousands.

value.zh: 孝惠皇帝諱衷，字正度，武帝第二子也。
value.en: Emperor Hui, whose personal name was Sima Zhong and courtesy name Zhengdu, was Emperor Wu’s second son.
value.literal: The Filial and Kind Emperor, taboo name Zhong, courtesy name Zhengdu, was the second son of Emperor Wu.

value.zh: 泰始三年，立爲皇太子，時年九歲。
value.en: In 267, when he was nine years old, he was named heir apparent.
value.literal: In the third year of Taishi, he was established as crown prince; at the time he was nine sui.

value.zh: 太熙元年四月己酉，武帝崩。
value.en: In the fourth month of the first year of Taixi, on the day jiyou, Emperor Wu died.
value.literal: In the first year of Taixi, on the jiyou day of the fourth month, Emperor Wu died.

value.zh: 是日，皇太子即皇帝位，大赦，改元爲永熙。
value.en: That same day the heir apparent ascended the throne, ordered a general amnesty, and adopted the reign title Yongxi.
value.literal: That same day the crown prince assumed the imperial throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Yongxi.

value.zh: 尊皇后楊氏曰皇太后，立妃賈氏爲皇后。
value.en: Empress Yang was elevated to empress dowager, and his consort Lady Jia was installed as empress.
value.literal: The empress, Lady Yang, was honored as empress dowager; Consort Jia was established as empress.

value.zh: 八月庚申，以趙王倫爲征東將軍、都督徐兗二州諸軍事；
value.en: Prince Lun of Zhao was named general who conquers the east and given joint command over Xu and Yan;
value.literal: In the eighth month, on the gengshen day, Prince Lun of Zhao was made general who conquers the east and area commander for military affairs in Xu and Yan provinces;

value.zh: 河間王顒爲北中郎將，鎮鄴；
value.en: Prince Yong of Hejian became a northern camp general and garrisoned Ye;
value.literal: Prince Yong of Hejian was made general of the northern gentlemen of the household and stationed at Ye;

value.zh: 太子太師何劭爲都督豫州諸軍事，鎮許昌。
value.en: He Shao, the heir apparent’s grand preceptor, took command in Yu Province from a base at Xuchang.
value.literal: Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent He Shao was made area commander for military affairs in Yu Province and stationed at Xuchang.

value.zh: 徙長沙王乂爲常山王。
value.en: Prince Yi of Changsha was re-enfeoffed as prince of Changshan.
value.literal: Prince Yi of Changsha was transferred to be prince of Changshan.

value.zh: 己巳，進西陽公羕爵爲王。
value.en: Duke Yang of Xiyang was raised to princely rank.
value.literal: On the jisi day, Duke Yang of Xiyang was advanced in noble rank to prince.

value.zh: 辛未，立隴西世子越爲東海王。
value.en: Yue, heir of the house of Longxi, was created prince of Donghai.
value.literal: On the xinwei day, heir apparent Yue of Longxi was established as prince of Donghai.

value.zh: 三月，平東將軍、齊王冏起兵以討倫，傳檄州郡，屯于陽翟。
value.en: In the third month Prince Jiong of Qi, general who pacifies the east, mobilized against Prince Lun, circulated a call to arms through every province, and camped at Yangzhai.
value.literal: In the third month, General Who Pacifies the East, Prince Jiong of Qi, raised troops to attack Lun, transmitted proclamations to the provinces and commanderies, and encamped at Yangzhai.

value.zh: 征北大將軍、成都王穎，征西大將軍、河間王顒，常山王乂，豫州刺史李毅，兗州刺史王彥，南中郎將、新野公歆，皆舉兵應之，眾數十萬。
value.en: Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu and Grand General Who Campaigns North; Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian and Grand General Who Campaigns West; Sima Yi, Prince of Changshan; Li Yi, inspector of Yu Province; Wang Yan, inspector of Yan Province; and Xin, Duke of Xinye and General of the Southern Gentlemen-of-the-Household, all raised armies in response, mustering several hundred thousand men.
value.literal: General-in-chief who conquers the north, Prince Ying of Chengdu; general-in-chief who conquers the west, Prince Yong of Hejian; Prince Yi of Changshan; Inspector of Yu Province Li Yi; Inspector of Yan Province Wang Yan; General of the Southern Gentlemen of the Household, Duke Xin of Xinye—all raised troops in response; the hosts numbered several hundred thousand.

value.zh: 倫遣其將閭和出伊闕，張泓、孫輔出堮阪以距冏，孫會、士猗、許超出黃橋以距穎。
value.en: Prince Lun sent Lü He through the Yique pass, Zhang Hong and Sun Fu over the E ridge to block Prince Jiong, and Sun Hui, Shi Yi, and Xu Chao from Huang Bridge to stop Prince Ying.
value.literal: Lun dispatched his generals Lü He out of Yique, Zhang Hong and Sun Fu out of E Slope to resist Jiong, and Sun Hui, Shi Yi, and Xu Chao out of Huang Bridge to resist Ying.

value.zh: 及穎將趙驤、石超戰于湨水，會等大敗，棄軍走。
value.en: At the Ju River, Zhao Xiang and Shi Chao, serving Prince Ying, routed Sun Hui’s army, which broke and ran.
value.literal: When Ying’s generals Zhao Xiang and Shi Chao battled at the Ju River, Hui and the others were greatly defeated and abandoned the army and fled.

value.zh: 秋七月甲午，立吳王晏子國爲漢王，復封常山王乂爲長沙王。
value.en: On the jiawu day in the seventh month Sima Guo, son of Prince Yan of Wu, was created prince of Han, and Prince Yi was moved back from Changshan to the Changsha princedom.
value.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the jiawu day, Prince Yan of Wu’s son Guo was established as prince of Han; Prince Yi of Changshan was again enfeoffed as prince of Changsha.

value.zh: 十二月丁亥，詔曰：「天禍晉邦，冢嗣莫繼。
value.en: On the dinghai day in the twelfth month an edict began: “Heaven scourges Jin, and no son of mine survives to succeed.
value.literal: On the dinghai day of the twelfth month an edict stated: “Heaven has punished the Jin state; no heir succeeds.

value.zh: 成都王穎自在儲貳，政績虧損，四海失望，不可承重，其以王還第。
value.en: Prince Ying proved unfit while heir apparent and has forfeited the trust of the realm, so he must be stripped of the succession and sent home to his fief.
value.literal: Prince Ying of Chengdu, while heir, failed in government; within the four seas hope was disappointed; he cannot bear the heavy charge; let him return to his residence as a prince.

value.zh: 豫章王熾先帝愛子，令問日新，四海注意，今以爲皇太弟，以隆我晉邦。
value.en: Prince Chi of Yuzhang, the late emperor’s favorite, grows in reputation every day, and he shall be named imperial younger brother and heir to steady the house of Jin.
value.literal: Prince Chi of Yuzhang was the late emperor’s beloved son; his fair fame grows daily; within the four seas all eyes turn to him; now let him be made imperial younger brother and heir to uplift our Jin state.

value.zh: 以司空越爲太傅，與太宰顒夾輔朕躬。
value.en: Minister of Works Prince Yue is appointed grand tutor to work beside Grand Steward Yong in guiding the throne.
value.literal: Let Minister of Works Yue be made grand tutor, together with Grand Steward Yong to flank and assist my person.

value.zh: 司徒王戎參錄朝政，光祿大夫王衍爲尚書左僕射。
value.en: Wang Rong shall join in supervising policy, and Wang Yan shall take the left vice directorship of the secretariat.
value.literal: Let Minister of Education Wang Rong participate in recording court governance; Household Grandee Wang Yan is made left vice director of the secretariat.

value.zh: 安南將軍虓、安北將軍浚、平北將軍騰各守本鎮。
value.en: Generals Xiao, Jun, and Teng are ordered to hold their existing commands.
value.literal: General Who Pacifies the South Xiao, General Who Pacifies the North Jun, and General Who Pacifies the North Teng each guard their original garrisons.

value.zh: 高密王簡爲鎮南將軍，領司隸校尉，權鎮洛陽；
value.en: Prince Jian of Gaomi becomes general who guards the south and acting metropolitan superintendent at Luoyang.
value.literal: Prince Jian of Gaomi is made general who guards the south, concurrently metropolitan superintendent, acting in authority at Luoyang;

value.zh: 東中郎將模爲寧北將軍、都督冀州，鎮于鄴；
value.en: Sima Mo moves to general who guards the north with Ji Province command, based at Ye.
value.literal: General of the Household Gentlemen of the East Mo is made general who guards the north and area commander for Ji Province, stationed at Ye;

value.zh: 鎮南大將軍劉弘領荊州，以鎮南土。
value.en: Liu Hong, general-in-chief who guards the south, keeps order in Jing Province.
value.literal: General-in-chief Who Guards the South Liu Hong holds Jing Province to secure the south.

value.zh: 周馥、繆胤各還本部，百官皆復職。
value.en: Zhou Fu and Miao Yin go back to their posts, and every minister returns to duty.
value.literal: Zhou Fu and Miao Yin each return to their original commands; the hundred officials all resume their posts.

value.zh: 齊王冏前應還第，長沙王乂輕陷重刑，封其子紹爲樂平縣王，以奉其嗣。
value.en: Prince Jiong ought long ago to have been sent to his domain, and Prince Yi suffered a cruel death, so enfeoff his son Shao as prince of Leping to preserve his line.
value.literal: Prince Jiong of Qi should earlier have returned to his residence; Prince Yi of Changsha was lightly subjected to heavy punishment; enfeoff his son Shao as prince of Leping county to continue his line.

value.zh: 自頃戎車屢征，勞費人力，供御之物皆減三分之二，戶調田租三分減一。
value.en: Because armies have marched again and again, palace supplies are cut by two-thirds, and the poll tax and land rent are each reduced by a third.
value.literal: Recently war-chariots have repeatedly marched, exhausting men and resources; articles for the imperial household are all reduced by two-thirds; household levies and field rent are each reduced by one-third.

value.zh: 蠲除苛政，愛人務本。
value.en: Harsh statutes are swept away so the people may return to their fields.
value.literal: Harsh government is remitted; the people are cherished and the root is sought.

value.zh: 清通之後，當還東京。」
value.en: Once peace is restored, the court will return to Luoyang.”
value.literal: After the realm is cleared and at peace, we shall return to the eastern capital.”

value.zh: 大赦，改元。
value.en: The edict ended with a general amnesty and a new reign title.
value.literal: A general amnesty; the era name was changed.

value.zh: 以河間王顒都督中外諸軍事。
value.en: Prince Yong of Hejian received overall command of every army.
value.literal: Prince Yong of Hejian was made area commander for all military affairs within and without.

value.zh: 月五星犯列舍經星變附見
value.en: The Moon and the Five Planets Transgressing the Lodges and Classical Stars, with Supplementary Notes on Celestial Portents.
value.literal: Transgressions of the Moon and the Five Planets against the Lodges and Classical Stars; appended observations on anomalies.

value.zh: 太安元年四月，彗星晝見。
value.en: Tai’an 1 April daytime comet.
value.literal: In Tai’an 1 fourth month a comet appeared by day.

value.zh: 二年三月，彗星見東方，指三台。
value.en: Tai’an 2 March eastern comet.
value.literal: In Tai’an 2 third month a comet appeared in the east pointing at Three Steps.

value.zh: 占曰：「兵喪之象。
value.en: The prognostication said, "It is the image of war and mourning.
value.literal: The omen-text says: “Image of armies and mourning.

value.zh: 三台為三公。」
value.en: The Three Terraces are the Three Dukes."
value.literal: Three Steps mean Three Dukes.

value.zh: 三年正月，東海王越執太尉、長沙王乂，張方又殺之。
value.en: Yue arrested Yi; Fang killed him.
value.literal: In the third year’s first month Prince Donghai Yue seized Grand Commandant Prince Changsha Yi and Zhang Fang murdered him.

value.zh: 安平獻王孚
value.en: Prince Xian of Anping, Sima Fu.
value.literal: Prince Fu of Anping with posthumous title Xian (section heading).

value.zh: 弈至黃門郎，先望卒。
value.en: Yi rose to yellow-gate gentleman but died before his father.
value.literal: Yi reached Yellow Gate Gentleman and died before Wang.

value.zh: 整亦早亡。
value.en: Zheng likewise died young.
value.literal: Zheng also died young.

value.zh: 以弈子奇襲爵。
value.en: The title passed to Yi's son Qi.
value.literal: By Yi's son Qi the noble rank was inherited.

value.zh: 奇亦好畜聚，不知紀極，遣三部使到交廣商貨，為有司所奏，太康九年，詔貶為三縱亭侯。
value.en: Qi also delighted in hoarding wealth without limit, sending three divisions of agents to trade in Jiao and Guang; after officials memorialized against him, an edict in Taikang year nine demoted him to Marquis of Sanzong Precinct.
value.literal: Qi also delighted in hoarding wealth without limit, sending three divisions of agents to trade in Jiao and Guang; after officials memorialized against him, an edict in Taikang year nine demoted him to Marquis of Sanzong Precinct.

value.zh: 更以章武王威為望嗣。
value.en: The throne then named Sima Wei of Zhangwu as Wang's heir.
value.literal: Next Prince Wei of Zhangwu was made Wang's successor.

value.zh: 後威誅，復立奇為棘陽王以嗣望。
value.en: After Wei's execution Qi was restored as Prince of Jiyang to continue Wang's line.
value.literal: Later when Wei was executed, Qi was again established as Prince of Jiyang to succeed Wang.

value.zh: 隨穆王整，兄弈卒，以整為世子。
value.en: When Yi died Zheng became heir of the Yiyang house.
value.literal: Prince Mu of Sui, Zheng—when elder brother Yi died Zheng was made heir apparent.

value.zh: 曆南中郎將，封清泉侯，先父望薨，追贈冠軍將軍。
value.en: He commanded southern gentlemen and held Qingquan marquis but predeceased Sima Wang; upon Wang's death the court posthumously named him Champion General.
value.literal: He successively held General of the Southern Gentlemen, was enfeoffed Marquis of Qingquan; he died before his father Wang; when Wang died he was posthumously invested Champion General.

value.zh: 武帝以義陽國一縣追封為隨縣王。
value.en: Emperor Wu carved out Sui county from Yiyang for his posthumous princedom.
value.literal: Emperor Wu used one county of the Yiyang state to posthumously enfeoff him as Prince of Sui county.

value.zh: 子邁嗣。
value.en: Mai succeeded him.
value.literal: Son Mai succeeded.

value.zh: 太康九年，以義陽之平林益邁為隨郡王。
value.en: In 288 Yiyang's Pinglin canton enlarged Mai's domain to prince of Sui commandery.
value.literal: In the ninth year of Taikang Pinglin of Yiyang was added to enlarge Mai as Prince of Sui commandery.

value.zh: 輔弟翼
value.en: Yi—Fu's younger brother.
value.literal: Fu di Yi.

value.zh: 翼字子世，少曆顯位，官至武賁中郎將。
value.en: Sima Yi, styled Zishi, rose young to major among the palace guards.
value.literal: Yi courtesy Zishi in youth successively held eminent posts and reached Major of the Household Guards.

value.zh: 武帝未受禪而卒，以兄邕之支子承為嗣，封南宮縣王。
value.en: He died before the Wei-Jin transition; Yong's collateral heir Cheng took Nangong county.
value.literal: Before Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he died; Yong's cadet son Cheng was appointed successor as Prince of Nangong county.

value.zh: 薨，子祐嗣立，承遂無後。
value.en: When Cheng died You continued the line, ending Cheng's branch.
value.literal: He died; son You succeeded and Cheng thereby had no posterity.

value.zh: 翼弟下邳獻王晃
value.en: Huang, Prince Xian of Xiapi—Yi's younger brother.
value.literal: Yi di Xiapi Offering Wang Huang.

value.zh: 及吳平，太康初詔復爵。
value.en: Taikang restored his rank after Wu fell.
value.literal: When Wu pacified Taikang early edict restored noble.

value.zh: 有司奏封江陽王，帝曰：「睦退靜思愆，改修其德，今有爵土，不但以赦。
value.en: Relevant offices memorialized enfeoff Jiangyang prince emperor said 'Mu retiring quiet pondering faults reform cultivating virtue now possessing noble territory not only because amnesty.
value.literal: Relevant offices memorialized enfeoff Jiangyang prince emperor said 'Mu retiring quiet pondering faults reform cultivating virtue now possessing noble territory not only because amnesty.

value.zh: 江陽險遠，其以高陽郡封之。」
value.en: Jiangyang peril remote therefore use Gaoyang commandery enfeoff him.'
value.literal: Jiangyang peril remote therefore use Gaoyang commandery enfeoff him.'

value.zh: 乃封為高陽王。
value.en: He became prince of Gaoyang.
value.literal: Thereupon enfeoffed Prince of Gaoyang.

value.zh: 元康元年，為宗正。
value.en: Yuankang named him imperial clan director.
value.literal: Yuankang year one became Grand Director of Imperial Clan.

value.zh: 薨於位，世子蔚早卒，孫毅立。
value.en: He died in post; grandson Yi followed after heir died young.
value.literal: Died in office heir apparent Wei died early grandson Yi succeeded.

value.zh: 拜散騎侍郎，永嘉中沒于石勒，
value.en: Yi fell to Shi Le during Yongjia.
value.literal: Appointed irregular cavalry gentleman middle Yongjia lost to Shi Le.

value.zh: 隆安元年，詔以譙敬王恬次子恢之子文深繼毅後。
value.en: In the first year of Long'an, the court assigned Wenshen from Huizhi's line to continue Yi.
value.literal: In the first year of Long'an, Edict appointed Prince Jing Tian second son Huizhi son Wenshen continuing Yi posterity.

value.zh: 立五年，薨，無嗣，復以高密王純之子法蓮繼之。
value.en: Five years later Falian continued the extinct line from Gaomi house.
value.literal: Established five years died without heirs again using Gaomi prince Chun son Falian continuing him.

value.zh: 宋受禪，國除。
value.en: Liu Song abolished the principality.
value.literal: When Song accepted abdication state abolished.

value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 湣懷太子遹，字熙祖，惠帝長子，母曰謝才人。
value.en: Sima Yu, styled Xizu, was Emperor Hui's firstborn—his mother was Lady Xie of Talented rank.
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.

value.zh: 幼而聰慧，武帝愛之，恆在左右。
value.en: Wu Di doted on the bright boy and kept him always near.
value.literal: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.

value.zh: 嘗與諸皇子共戲殿上，惠帝來朝，執諸皇子手，次至太子，帝曰：「是汝兒也。」
value.en: Once he was playing on the palace steps with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience, he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, the emperor said, 'This is your son.'
value.literal: Once he was playing on the palace steps with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, Emperor Wu said, 'This is your son.'

value.zh: 惠帝乃止。
value.en: Hui broke off his greeting.
value.literal: Emperor Hui thereupon stopped.

value.zh: 宮中嘗夜失火，武帝登樓望之。
value.en: A night blaze drew Wu Di to a high gallery.
value.literal: Once at night the palace caught fire; Emperor Wu climbed a tower to watch.

value.zh: 太子時年五歲，牽帝裾入暗中。
value.en: Five-year-old Yu pulled his grandfather into the dark.
value.literal: The crown prince was then five years old; he tugged the emperor's robe into the shadows.

value.zh: 帝問其故，太子曰：「暮夜倉卒，宜備非常，不宜令照見人君也。」
value.en: The crown prince said, "Suddenly at night one must guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face."
value.literal: The emperor asked why; the crown prince said, 'Suddenly at night one should guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face.'

value.zh: 由是奇之。
value.en: Wu Di marked him extraordinary.
value.literal: From this Wu Di marveled at him.

value.zh: 嘗從帝觀豕牢，言於帝曰：「豕甚肥，何不殺以享士，而使久費五穀？」
value.en: While watching the imperial sty he said to the emperor, "The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?"
value.literal: Once when following the emperor to view the pig pen he said to the emperor, 'The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?'

value.zh: 帝嘉其意，即使烹之。
value.en: Wu Di approved and had them slaughtered.
value.literal: The emperor praised his intent and at once ordered them cooked.

value.zh: 因撫其背，謂廷尉傅祗曰：「此兒當興我家。」
value.en: He stroked the boy's back and told Court Commandant Fu Zhi, "This child will bring prosperity to our house."
value.literal: He therefore stroked the boy's back and said to Court Commandant Fu Zhi, 'This child will bring prosperity to our house.'

value.zh: 嘗對群臣稱太子似宣帝，於是令譽流於天下。
value.en: He likened the heir to Sima Yi before court—reputation followed.
value.literal: He once declared before the assembled ministers that the crown prince resembled Emperor Xuan; thereafter praise of him spread through the realm.

value.zh: 孫惠
value.en: Sun Hui.
value.literal: Section heading: Sun Hui.

value.zh: 孫惠，字德施，吳國富陽人，吳豫章太守賁曾孫也。
value.en: Sun Hui, whose courtesy name was Deshi, came from Fuyang in the old state of Wu and was a great-grandson of Ben, the Yuzhang grand administrator who had served Wu.
value.literal: Sun Hui, courtesy name Deshi, was a native of Fuyang in the state of Wu; he was a great-grandson of Ben, who had been Grand Administrator of Yuzhang under Wu.

value.zh: 父祖並仕吳。
value.en: Both his father and his grandfather had served the Wu regime.
value.literal: His father and grandfather both held office in Wu.

value.zh: 惠口訥，好學有才識，州辟不就，寓居蕭沛之間。
value.en: He was awkward in speech but a devoted student, with real ability and insight. Though the provincial authorities tried to appoint him, he stayed out of office and lived for a time between Xiao and Pei.
value.literal: Hui was slow of tongue, loved learning, and had talent and judgment; the province summoned him but he did not take office, and he lodged between Xiao and Pei.

value.zh: 永甯初，赴齊王冏義，討趙王倫，以功封晉興縣侯，辟大司馬戶曹掾，轉東曹屬。
value.en: When Yongning began, he joined Sima Jiong, the Prince of Qi, in the loyalist campaign against Sima Lun, the Prince of Zhao. His service earned him the county marquisate of Jinxing, a post as clerk in the minister of war's revenue office, and then a place on the eastern staff.
value.literal: At the beginning of the Yongning era, he answered Prince of Qi Jiong's call to righteous arms and campaigned against Prince of Zhao Lun; for merit he was enfeoffed marquis of Jinxing County, appointed clerk in the Revenue Bureau of the Minister of War, then transferred to a subordinate post in the eastern bureau.

value.zh: 冏驕矜僭侈，天下失望。
value.en: Jiong grew haughty and overbearing, overstepping his rank and spending on a princely scale until the empire had lost faith in him.
value.literal: Jiong was arrogant, boastful, presumptuous, and extravagant; all under Heaven were disappointed in him.

value.zh: 惠獻言於冏，諷以五難、四不可，勸令歸籓，辭甚切至。
value.en: Sun Hui laid before him a carefully framed remonstrance—the 'five difficulties' and 'four impossibilities'—urging him to withdraw to his princely domain. The tone was urgent and uncompromising.
value.literal: Hui submitted advice to Jiong, using 'five difficulties' and 'four impossibilities' as indirect admonition, urging him to return to his fief; the wording was extremely blunt and thorough.

value.zh: 冏不納。
value.en: Jiong refused to listen.
value.literal: Jiong did not accept it.

value.zh: 惠懼罪，辭疾去。
value.en: Fearing reprisals, Sun Hui pleaded illness and slipped away.
value.literal: Hui feared punishment, pleaded illness, and departed.

value.zh: 頃之，冏果敗。
value.en: Soon afterward Jiong fell, exactly as he had warned.
value.literal: Before long, Jiong indeed was defeated.

value.zh: 成都王穎薦惠為大將軍參軍、領奮威將軍、白沙督。
value.en: Sima Ying, the Prince of Chengdu, then recommended him as an adviser on the grand general's staff, with the concurrent titles of General Who Rouses Might and commander of the Baisha garrison.
value.literal: Prince of Chengdu Ying recommended Hui as staff adviser to the grand general, concurrently General Who Rouses Might, and commander at Baisha.

value.zh: 是時，穎將征長沙王乂，以陸機為前鋒都督。
value.en: Ying was preparing to move against Sima Yi, the Prince of Changsha, and named Lu Ji to lead the van.
value.literal: At this time Ying was about to campaign against Prince of Changsha Yi and appointed Lu Ji as commander of the vanguard.

value.zh: 惠與機同鄉里，憂其致禍，勸機讓都督于王粹。
value.en: As a townsman of Lu Ji, Sun Hui worried the appointment would destroy him and urged him to step aside in favor of Wang Cui.
value.literal: Hui was from the same home region as Ji; fearing that Ji would bring disaster on himself, he urged Ji to yield the commander's post to Wang Cui.

value.zh: 及機兄弟被戮，惠甚傷恨之。
value.en: When Lu Ji and his brothers were put to death, Sun Hui mourned them bitterly.
value.literal: When Ji and his brothers were executed, Hui deeply grieved and resented it.

value.zh: 時惠又擅殺穎牙門將梁俊，懼罪，因改姓名以遁。
value.en: He had already killed Liang Jun, one of Ying's gate generals, without orders. Dreading the consequences, he took a new identity and went into hiding.
value.literal: At that time Hui had also on his own authority killed Liang Jun, a gate-guard general under Ying; fearing punishment, he changed his name and fled into hiding.

value.zh: 序
value.en: Preface
value.literal: Preface

value.zh: 尋徵為御史中丞，未拜，復為侍中。
value.en: He was soon summoned as assistant chief of the Censorate but, before taking up the post, was again named Palace Attendant.
value.literal: Soon he was summoned as Palace Assistant Clerk of the Censorate; before he took office he again became Palace Attendant.

value.zh: 河間王顒、成都王穎舉兵向京都，以討長沙王乂，大駕次於城東。
value.en: Prince of Hejian Sima Yong and Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying marched on the capital against Prince of Changsha Sima Yi; the imperial train halted east of the walls.
value.literal: Prince of Hejian Sima Yong and Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying raised troops toward the capital to strike Prince of Changsha Sima Yi; the imperial carriage halted east of the city.

value.zh: 乂言於眾曰：「今日西討，欲誰為都督乎？」
value.en: Yi asked the gathered officers: "For this western campaign, whom do you want as overall commander?"
value.literal: Yi said to the assembly: "Today we march west—whom do you wish as commander?"

value.zh: 六軍之士皆曰：「願嵇侍中戮力前驅，死猶生也。」
value.en: The men of the six armies shouted: "We want Palace Attendant Ji in the van—we would rather die beside him than live elsewhere!"
value.literal: The troops of the six armies said: "We wish Palace Attendant Ji to strain every nerve in the vanguard—to die would be as living."

value.zh: 遂拜紹使持節、平西將軍。
value.en: So Shao received the credential-bearing commission and the title General Who Pacifies the West.
value.literal: Shao was therefore appointed commissioner bearing credentials and General Who Pacifies the West.

value.zh: 屬乂被執，紹復為侍中。
value.en: After Yi was captured, Shao returned to the post of Palace Attendant.
value.literal: When Yi was seized, Shao again became Palace Attendant.

value.zh: 公王以下皆詣鄴謝罪於穎，紹等咸見廢黜，免為庶人。
value.en: Every prince and noble went to Ye to submit to Sima Ying; Shao and his peers were stripped of office and reduced to common status.
value.literal: All ranks from dukes and princes downward went to Ye to apologize to Ying; Shao and others were all cashiered and reduced to commoners.

value.zh: 尋而朝廷復有北征之役，征紹，復其爵位。
value.en: Soon the court launched another northern campaign, recalled Shao, and restored his titles.
value.literal: Soon the court mounted another northern expedition and summoned Shao, restoring his noble rank.

value.zh: 紹以天子蒙塵，承詔馳詣行在所。
value.en: With the emperor on the run, Shao took the edict and rode hard for the imperial headquarters.
value.literal: Because the Son of Heaven was in exile, Shao received the edict and galloped to the temporary residence.

value.zh: 值王師敗績于蕩陰，百官及侍衛莫不散潰，唯紹儼然端冕，以身捍衛，兵交御輦，飛箭雨集，紹遂被害於帝側，血濺御服，天子深哀歎之。
value.en: At Dangyin the imperial army collapsed; ministers and guards fled—only Shao, erect in full court dress, threw himself between the emperor and the blades. Weapons clashed around the carriage, arrows fell like rain, and Shao died at the sovereign's side, his blood staining the imperial robe while the emperor wept over him.
value.literal: When the royal army was routed at Dangyin, officials and guards scattered in panic—only Shao, unmoved in full court garb, shielded the ruler with his body; weapons clashed about the imperial carriage and arrows fell like rain; Shao was thus slain beside the emperor, his blood splashing the imperial robe, and the Son of Heaven mourned him deeply.

value.zh: 及事定，左右欲浣衣，帝曰：「此嵇侍中血，勿去。」
value.en: Afterward, servants wanted to launder the robe; the emperor said: "That is Palace Attendant Ji's blood—leave it."
value.literal: When things settled, attendants wished to wash the robe; the emperor said: "This is Palace Attendant Ji's blood—do not remove it."

value.zh: 齊王冏辟為征西參軍，襲爵武昌鄉侯。
value.en: Prince of Qi Sima Jiong appointed him adjutant on the western campaign, and he inherited the village marquisate at Wuchang.
value.literal: Prince of Qi Sima Jiong summoned him as adjutant on the western expedition and he inherited the village marquisate of Wuchang.

value.zh: 長沙王乂召為驃騎記室督、尚書郎。
value.en: Prince of Changsha Sima Yi appointed him recorder-in-chief to the chief commander and Gentleman of the Secretariat.
value.literal: Prince of Changsha Sima Yi summoned him as recorder-in-chief to the chief commander and Gentleman of the Secretariat.

value.zh: 乂與成都王穎交戰，穎軍轉盛，尚書郎旦出督戰，夜還理事。
value.en: When Yi clashed with Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying, Ying's forces gained ground; the Secretariat gentlemen rode out at dawn to supervise the fighting and returned after dark to manage paperwork.
value.literal: Yi fought Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying; Ying's army grew stronger; the Secretariat gentlemen went out at dawn to oversee battle and returned at night to handle affairs.

value.zh: 含言於乂曰：「昔魏武每有軍事，增置掾屬。
value.en: Han urged Yi: "Whenever Emperor Wu of Wei faced war, he expanded aide posts.
value.literal: Han said to Yi: "In old days whenever Wu of Wei had military affairs, he added aides and staff.

value.zh: 青龍二年，尚書令陳矯以有軍務，亦奏增郎。
value.en: In Qinglong 2, Director of the Secretariat Chen Jiao, citing military business, likewise petitioned for added Secretariat gentlemen.
value.literal: In the second year of Qinglong, Director of the Secretariat Chen Jiao, because there were military matters, also memorialized to add gentlemen.

value.zh: 今奸逆四逼，王路擁塞，倒懸之急，不復過此。
value.en: Today rebels ring us on every side; the imperial highways clog; we hang by our heels—nothing could be more urgent.
value.literal: Now treason presses from four sides; the royal road is blocked; the urgency of hanging upside down could not be greater.

value.zh: 但居曹理事，尚須增郎，況今都官中騎三曹晝出督戰，夜還理事，一人兩役，內外廢乏。
value.en: Stationery offices still need extra hands in quiet times—how much more when the Capital, Palace, and Cavalry sections march out by day to direct combat and draft orders by night; one officer pulling double duty exhausts both camp and capital.
value.literal: Yet merely sitting in headquarters handling business still requires added gentlemen—how much more now when the Capital Bureau, Palace Bureau, and Cavalry Bureau go out by day to oversee battle and return by night to handle affairs—one man bearing two duties, inner and outer alike exhausted.

value.zh: 含謂今有十萬人，都督各有主帥，推轂授綏，委付大將，不宜復令台僚雜與其間。」
value.en: Han argues that with a hundred thousand troops under distinct commanders—each lieutenant invested with drum and reins—a chief general should hold the line; secretariat aides ought not clutter the chain of command."
value.literal: Han holds that with one hundred thousand men, each command has its commander; push the carriage and hand the reins—entrust it to a great general; you should not again let terrace aides mix among them."

value.zh: 乂從之，乃增郎及令史。
value.en: Yi agreed and expanded the Secretariat rolls with added gentlemen and clerks.
value.literal: Yi followed him and added gentlemen and clerks.

value.zh: 冏令曰：「得前後白事，具意，輒別思量也。」
value.en: Jiong replied: "I have your successive memorials in full; I will weigh them separately."
value.literal: Jiong ordered: "I have received your successive reports in full; I will consider them separately."

value.zh: 會長沙王乂至，於冏案上見豹箋，謂冏曰：「小子離間骨肉，何不銅駝下打殺！」
value.en: When Prince of Changsha Sima Yi arrived, he spotted Bao's paper on Jiong's desk and snarled: "This whelp sows strife in the royal family—beat him to death under the bronze camels!"
value.literal: When Prince of Changsha Sima Yi arrived, he saw Bao's memorandum on Jiong's desk and said to Jiong: "This boy sows discord among flesh and blood—why not beat him to death under the bronze camels!"

value.zh: 冏既不能嘉豹之策，遂納乂言，乃奏豹曰：「臣忿奸凶肆逆，皇祚顛墜，與成都、長沙、新野共興義兵，安復社稷，唯欲戮力皇家，與親親宗室腹心從事，此臣夙夜自誓，無負神明。
value.en: Jiong spurned Bao's advice and took Yi's bait, memorializing: "Your servant burns as traitors overturn heaven; with Chengdu, Changsha, and Xinyue I raised righteous armies to heal the altars—my vow night and day is to exhaust myself for the throne alongside true kinsmen—may the spirits witness me.
value.literal: Jiong could not embrace Bao's plan; he accepted Yi's words and therefore memorialized concerning Bao: "Your subject resents how villains ran riot and the imperial fortune toppled; with Chengdu, Changsha, and Xinyue he jointly raised loyal troops to restore the altars—my sole wish is to strain every nerve for the royal house and work heart to heart with close imperial kin—this is what your subject swears day and night, not betraying the spirits.

value.zh: 而主簿王豹比有白事，敢造異端，謂臣忝備宰相，必遘危害，慮在一旦，不祥之聲可蹻足而待，欲臣與成都分陝為伯，盡出籓王。
value.en: Yet chief clerk Wang Bao keeps forwarding heterodox schemes—claiming this minister, unworthy though I am of the chancellorship, faces doom within days and ill omens before we lift a foot—demanding that I split the realm with Chengdu like the ancient elders and banish every prince to his fief.
value.literal: Yet chief clerk Wang Bao has repeatedly submitted reports daring to craft strange heterodoxy, claiming your subject, shamefully filling the role of chief minister, is sure to meet harm and that peril waits within the day—inauspicious cries may arrive as soon as one lifts a heel—wishing your subject with Chengdu to divide Shan as elders and send out all the feudal princes.

value.zh: 上誣聖朝鑒御之威，下長妖惑，疑阻眾心，噂背憎，巧賣兩端，訕上謗下，讒內間外，遘惡導奸，坐生猜嫌。
value.en: He traduces imperial majesty above while sowing panic below; he sets minds doubting and breeds whispered hatred; he plays both ends, mocks superiors and baits inferiors, slanders court and alienates the regions—drawing villains together until suspicion festers.
value.literal: Above he slanders the sagely court's awesome governance; below he fosters weird delusion, doubts and blocks the host of hearts—backbiting and hatred; he craftily sells to both sides, mocks above and slanders below, slanders within and estranges without—encountering evil and guiding villainy, sitting and breeding suspicion.

value.zh: 昔孔丘匡魯，乃誅少正；
value.en: Confucius restored Lu by executing Shaozheng Mao—
value.literal: In old days Confucius restored Lu and thus executed Shaozheng Mao;

value.zh: 子產相鄭，先戮鄧析，誠以交亂名實，若趙高詭怪之類也。
value.en: Zichan governed Zheng and executed Deng Xi first—both struck down men who twisted name and fact like Zhao Gao's breed.
value.literal: Zichan served Zheng as minister and first executed Deng Xi—truly because they confused name with reality, like Zhao Gao's deceitful sort.

value.zh: 豹為臣不忠不順不義，輒敕都街考竟，以明邪正。」
value.en: Wang Bao is disloyal, unfilial, unjust—I order him beaten to death in the capital street to mark the line between treason and right."
value.literal: Bao as a subject was disloyal, unfilial, and unjust—your subject orders him interrogated to death in the capital avenue to clarify evil and upright."

value.zh: 豹將死，曰：「懸吾頭大司馬門，見兵之攻齊也。」
value.en: Facing death Bao said: "Hang my head on the Grand Marshal's gate—you will see armies march against Qi."
value.literal: As Bao was about to die he said: "Hang my head at the Grand Marshal's gate—watch the armies attack Qi."

value.zh: 眾庶冤之。
value.en: The crowd counted him wronged.
value.literal: The common people thought him wronged.

value.zh: 俄而冏敗。
value.en: Soon Sima Jiong fell.
value.literal: Soon Jiong was defeated.

value.zh: 劉沈，字道真，燕國薊人也。
value.en: Liu Shen, courtesy name Daozhen, came from Ji in Yan.
value.literal: Liu Shen, courtesy name Daozhen, was a man of Ji in the state of Yan.

value.zh: 世為北州名族。
value.en: His clan ranked among the north's great families for generations.
value.literal: For generations his clan was a distinguished house of the northern provinces.

value.zh: 少仕州郡，博學好古。
value.en: Youth brought minor provincial posts; he read widely and revered antiquity.
value.literal: In youth he served in provincial posts; he was broadly learned and loved antiquity.

value.zh: 太保衛瓘辟為掾，領本邑大中正。
value.en: Grand Mentor Wei Guan took him on as an aide and put him in charge of local personnel appraisal as senior rectifier.
value.literal: Grand Mentor Wei Guan summoned him as aide and assigned him concurrent duty as senior rectifier for his native district.

value.zh: 敦儒道，愛賢能，進霍原為二品，及申理張華，皆辭旨明峻，為當時所稱。
value.en: He championed scholarship, prized talent, promoted Huo Yuan to the second grade, and defended Zhang Hua—each memorial lucid and uncompromising, earning wide acclaim.
value.literal: He honored Confucian teaching and loved worthy talent; advancing Huo Yuan to the second rank and arguing Zhang Hua's case—all were marked by bright, stern wording and praised by contemporaries.

value.zh: 齊王冏輔政，引為左長史，遷侍中。
value.en: Prince of Qi Sima Jiong, while directing government, brought Liu Shen in as Left Senior Clerk and soon promoted him to Palace Attendant.
value.literal: When Prince of Qi Sima Jiong directed affairs, he summoned Shen as Left Senior Clerk and promoted him to Palace Attendant.

value.zh: 于時李流亂蜀，詔沈以侍中、假節，統益州刺史羅尚、梁州刺史許雄等以討流。
value.en: While Li Liu ravaged Shu, the throne named Liu Shen Palace Attendant with credential staff to coordinate Luo Shang of Yi Province, Xu Xiong of Liang Province, and others against him.
value.literal: At that time Li Liu rebelled in Shu; an edict appointed Shen as Palace Attendant with credential staff to oversee Inspector of Yi Province Luo Shang, Inspector of Liang Province Xu Xiong, and others to strike Liu.

value.zh: 行次長安，河間王顒請留沉為軍司，遣席薳代之。
value.en: His march paused at Chang'an; Prince of Hejian Sima Yong asked to keep Liu Shen as army marshal and dispatched Xi Yuan to replace him on campaign.
value.literal: Marching, he halted at Chang'an; Prince of Hejian Yong requested to retain Shen as army marshal and sent Xi Yuan to replace him.

value.zh: 後領雍州刺史。
value.en: He later added concurrent duty as Inspector of Yong Province.
value.literal: Later he concurrently served as Inspector of Yong Province.

value.zh: 及張昌作亂，詔顒遣沉將州兵萬人並征西府五千人，自藍田關以討之，顒不奉詔。
value.en: When Zhang Chang rose, an edict told Yong to send Liu Shen with ten thousand Yong troops and five thousand western expedition troops through Lantian Pass—Yong ignored it.
value.literal: When Zhang Chang rebelled, an edict ordered Yong to send Shen leading ten thousand provincial troops plus five thousand from the western expedition headquarters through Lantian Pass to attack him; Yong did not obey the edict.

value.zh: 沉自領州兵至藍田，顒又逼奪其眾。
value.en: Liu Shen drove the provincial army to Lantian anyway; Yong seized those troops from him.
value.literal: Shen himself led provincial troops to Lantian; Yong again pressed and seized his forces.

value.zh: 長沙王乂命沉將武吏四百人還州。
value.en: Prince of Changsha Sima Yi ordered Liu Shen to march four hundred armed clerks back to Yong Province.
value.literal: Prince of Changsha Yi ordered Shen to lead four hundred martial clerks back to the province.

value.zh: 張方既逼京都，王師屢敗，王瑚、祖逖言於乂曰：「劉沈忠義果毅，雍州兵力足制河間，宜啟上詔與沈，使發兵襲顒，顒窘急，必召張方以自救，此計之良也。」
value.en: With Zhang Fang threatening Luoyang and imperial armies failing, Wang Hu and Zu Ti urged Sima Yi: "Liu Shen is loyal and bold; Yong Province can pin Prince of Hejian—petition the emperor to order Shen to strike Yong; Yong, desperate, will recall Zhang Fang—that breaks the siege."
value.literal: Once Zhang Fang threatened the capital and the royal army repeatedly lost, Wang Hu and Zu Ti said to Yi: "Liu Shen is loyal, righteous, resolute, and daring; Yong Province's military strength is enough to control Hejian—you should memorialize the throne to issue an edict to Shen ordering him to raise troops and strike Yong; Yong, embarrassed and pressed, is sure to summon Zhang Fang to rescue himself—this is an excellent plan."

value.zh: 乂從之。
value.en: Yi agreed.
value.literal: Yi followed them.

value.zh: 沈奉詔馳檄四境，合七郡之眾及守防諸軍、塢壁甲士萬餘人，以安定太守衛博、新平太守張光、安定功曹皇甫澹為先登，襲長安。
value.en: Liu Shen rode the edict to rally seven counties, garrisons, and fortress troops—more than ten thousand—then struck Chang'an with Wei Bo of Anding, Zhang Guang of Xinping, and Huangfu Dan leading the van.
value.literal: Shen received the edict and galloped proclamations through the four borders, assembling the hosts of seven counties together with garrison defenders and fort warriors—over ten thousand—and with Administrator of Anding Wei Bo, Administrator of Xinping Zhang Guang, and merit evaluator Huangfu Dan of Anding as van bearers, attacked Chang'an.

value.zh: 顒時頓于鄭縣之高平亭，為東軍聲援，聞沈兵起，還鎮渭城，遣督護虞夔率步騎萬餘人逆沈於好畤。
value.en: Sima Yong had camped at Gaoping Pavilion to screen eastern reinforcements; hearing Liu Shen move, he pulled back to Weicheng and sent Yu Kui with ten thousand horse and foot to intercept Shen at Haozhi.
value.literal: Yong at that time was halted at Gaoping Pavilion in Zheng County as eastern-army support; hearing Shen's troops had risen, he returned to guard Weicheng and sent Protector Yu Kui with over ten thousand infantry and cavalry to oppose Shen at Haozhi.

value.zh: 接戰，夔眾敗，顒大懼，退入長安，果急呼張方。
value.en: Kui lost the engagement; Yong fled into Chang'an in panic and screamed for Zhang Fang.
value.literal: They engaged in battle; Kui's host was defeated; Yong was greatly afraid and withdrew into Chang'an, urgently summoning Zhang Fang.

value.zh: 沈渡渭而壘，顒每遣兵出鬥，輒不利，沈乘勝攻之，使澹、博以精甲五千，從長安門而入，力戰至顒帳下。
value.en: Liu Shen crossed the Wei and walled up; Yong's sallies failed again and again—Shen pressed the advantage, sending Huangfu Dan and Wei Bo with five thousand elite armored men through Chang'an Gate to fight through to Yong's headquarters.
value.literal: Shen crossed the Wei and built ramparts; Yong repeatedly sent troops out to fight but consistently failed; Shen exploited victory to attack him, ordering Dan and Bo with five thousand picked armored troops to enter through Chang'an Gate and fight fiercely to Yong's command tent.

value.zh: 沈軍來遲，顒軍見澹等無繼，氣益倍。
value.en: Shen's main body arrived late; Yong's men saw Dan had no backup and doubled their fighting spirit.
value.literal: Shen's army arrived late; Yong's troops saw Dan and others had no reinforcements and their morale doubled.

value.zh: 馮翊太守張輔率眾救顒，橫擊之，大戰於府門，博父子皆死之，澹又被擒。
value.en: Zhang Fu of Fengyi slammed into Shen's flank before Yong's yamen—Wei Bo and his son died there; Huangfu Dan was taken.
value.literal: Administrator of Fengyi Zhang Fu led a host to rescue Yong and struck them sideways; they fought a great battle at the headquarters gate—Bo and his son both died in it, and Dan was also captured.

value.zh: 顒奇澹壯勇，將活之。
value.en: Yong admired Dan's courage and meant to spare him.
value.literal: Yong marveled at Dan's bravery and wished to spare him.

value.zh: 澹不為之屈，於是見殺。
value.en: Dan refused to bend, so Yong executed him.
value.literal: Dan would not yield and was therefore executed.

value.zh: 沈軍遂敗，率余卒屯于故營。
value.en: Shen's line collapsed; he gathered survivors at the old camp.
value.literal: Shen's army was thus defeated; he led surviving troops to camp at the old stockade.

value.zh: 張方遣其將敦偉夜至，沈軍大驚而潰，與麾下百餘人南遁，為陳倉令所執。
value.en: Zhang Fang's officer Dun Wei struck by night; Shen's men broke and fled—he escaped south with a hundred riders until the Chencang magistrate seized him.
value.literal: Zhang Fang sent his general Dun Wei by night; Shen's army panicked and scattered; with over a hundred followers he fled south and was seized by the magistrate of Chencang.

value.zh: 沈謂顒曰：「夫知己之顧輕，在三之節重，不可違君父之詔，量強弱以苟全。
value.en: Liu Shen told Yong: "Private kindness weighs little beside the three great bonds—I cannot defy sovereign and father to save myself by calculating odds.
value.literal: Shen said to Yong: "Though favor from a confidant may be light, the obligation of the three bonds weighs heavily—I may not disobey father and lord's edicts nor gauge strength and weakness to preserve myself cheaply.

value.zh: 投袂之日，期之必死，菹醢之戮，甘之如薺。」
value.en: The day I raised arms I accepted death—mincing and saucing would taste to me like spring greens."
value.literal: The day I cast aside my sleeve I fixed my heart on death—pickling and mincing punishment I would relish like shepherd's purse."

value.zh: 辭義慷慨，見者哀之。
value.en: He spoke with blazing conviction; onlookers wept for him.
value.literal: His words were righteous and stirring; those who saw pitied him.

value.zh: 顒怒，鞭之而後腰斬。
value.en: Yong had him flogged, then cut in half at the waist.
value.literal: Yong angrily flogged him and then cut him in two at the waist.

value.zh: 有識者以顒干上犯順，虐害忠義，知其滅亡不久也。
value.en: Thoughtful observers saw Yong defying heaven and torturing loyal men—they knew he would not last.
value.literal: Knowing men considered that Yong had offended superiors and violated propriety and cruelly harmed loyalty and righteousness—they knew his destruction would come soon.

value.zh: 序
value.en: Preface
value.literal: Preface

value.zh: 及齊王冏輔政，攄與左思俱為記室督。
value.en: When Prince Qi Sima Jiong directed the regime, Cao Shu and Zuo Si jointly supervised the secretariat.
value.literal: When Prince of Qi Sima Jiong assisted the government, Shu together with Zuo Si both served as supervisors of the secretariat.

value.zh: 冏嘗從容問攄曰：「天子為賊臣所逼，莫有能奮。
value.en: Jiong once calmly asked Shu: 'The Son of Heaven was coerced by traitorous ministers; none could rouse himself.
value.literal: Jiong once calmly asked Shu: 'The Son of Heaven was coerced by traitorous ministers; none could rouse himself.

value.zh: 吾率四海義兵興復王室，今入輔朝廷，匡振時艱，或有勸吾還國，於卿意如何？」
value.en: I led righteous troops from within the four seas to restore the royal house; now I enter and assist the court, aiding the hardship of the times—some urge me to return to my princedom; what is your thought?'
value.literal: I led righteous troops from within the four seas to restore the royal house; now I enter and assist the court, aiding the hardship of the times—some urge me to return to my princedom; what is your thought?'

value.zh: 攄曰：「蕩平國賊，匡復帝祚，古今人臣之功未有如大王之盛也。
value.en: Shu said: 'Sweeping away state rebels and restoring the imperial throne—among ministers through history none has achieved merit as great as the great king's.
value.literal: Shu said: 'Sweeping away state rebels and restoring the imperial throne—among ministers through history none has achieved merit as great as the great king's.

value.zh: 然道罔隆而不殺，物無盛而不衰，非唯人事，抑亦天理。
value.en: Yet the Way never rises without decline; nothing flourishes without fading—not only in human affairs but also in the pattern of Heaven.
value.literal: Yet the Way never rises without decline; nothing flourishes without fading—not only in human affairs but also in the pattern of Heaven.

value.zh: 竊預下問，敢不盡情。
value.en: Having received your humble inquiry below, how dare I not speak my whole mind.
value.literal: Having received your humble inquiry below, how dare I not speak my whole mind.

value.zh: 願大王居高慮危，在盈思沖，精選百官，存公屏欲，舉賢進善，務得其才，然後脂車秣馬，高揖歸籓，則上下同慶，攄等幸甚。」
value.en: I wish the great king, dwelling high, to think of peril; in fullness to think of emptiness; carefully select the hundred officials; preserve impartiality and restrain desire; promote the worthy and advance the good, striving to obtain true talent—then grease the carriage and feed the horses, bow deeply and return to your fief; then high and low alike will rejoice, and Shu and the rest will be greatly fortunate.'
value.literal: I wish the great king, dwelling high, to think of peril; in fullness to think of emptiness; carefully select the hundred officials; preserve impartiality and restrain desire; promote the worthy and advance the good, striving to obtain true talent—then grease the carriage and feed the horses, bow deeply and return to your fief; then high and low alike will rejoice, and Shu and the rest will be greatly fortunate.'

value.zh: 冏不納。
value.en: Sima Jiong brushed the counsel aside.
value.literal: Jiong did not accept the advice.

value.zh: 尋轉中書侍郎。
value.en: He soon moved to vice director of the Secretariat.
value.literal: Shortly he was transferred to vice director of the Secretariat.

value.zh: 長沙王乂以為驃騎司馬。
value.en: Prince Changsha Sima Yi named him staff marshal on the agile-cavalry command.
value.literal: Prince Changsha Sima Yi appointed him marshal for the General of Agile Cavalry.

value.zh: 乂敗，免官。
value.en: After Prince Changsha fell, Cao Shu lost his post.
value.literal: When Yi was defeated, [Shu] was dismissed from office.

value.zh: 因丁母憂。
value.en: He then withdrew to mourn his mother.
value.literal: Thereupon he observed mourning for his mother.

value.zh: 惠帝末，起為襄城太守，
value.en: Late in Emperor Hui's reign he returned as Xiangcheng prefect.
value.literal: At the end of Emperor Hui's reign he was raised up as Administrator of Xiangcheng.

value.zh: 唐禮：四時各以孟月享太廟，每室用太牢，季冬蠟祭之後，以辰日臘享於太廟，用牲如時祭。
value.en: Tang ritual: each season's first month, offerings at the Great Temple—tai lao per chamber. After twelfth-month wax and la, a chen-day la feast at the temple used seasonal victims.
value.literal: Tang rites: In each of the four seasons, in the first month of the season, offerings were made to the Great Ancestral Temple; for each chamber the great offering was used. After the wax sacrifices following the twelfth month's la rites, on a chen day a la offering was presented at the Great Temple, with victims as at the seasonal sacrifices.

value.zh: 三年一祫，以孟冬。
value.en: A he rite every three years, in mid-winter's opening month.
value.literal: Every three years a he sacrifice, in the first month of winter.

value.zh: 五年一禘，以孟夏。
value.en: A di rite every five years, in mid-summer's opening month.
value.literal: Every five years a di sacrifice, in the first month of summer.

value.zh: 又時享之日，修七祀於太廟西門內之道南：司命，戶以春，灶以夏；
value.en: On seasonal offering days the Seven Sacrifices were kept on the lane south of the temple's west gate—Spirit of Fate; Household Spirit in spring, Stove Spirit in summer;
value.literal: On days of seasonal offerings, the Seven Sacrifices were maintained on the road south within the western gate of the Great Temple: Spirit of Fate; the Household Spirit in spring, the Stove Spirit in summer;

value.zh: 門，厲以秋，行以冬，中溜則于季夏迎氣日祀之。
value.en: Gate and Pestilence Spirits in autumn, Road Spirit in winter; Central Gutter on the last-summer qi-reception day.
value.literal: the Gate Spirit and the Pestilence Spirit in autumn, the Road Spirit in winter; the Central Gutter was sacrificed on the day of receiving seasonal qi in the last month of summer.

value.zh: 若品物時新堪進御者，所司先送太常，與尚食相知，簡擇精好者，以滋味與新物相宜者配之。
value.en: Seasonal delicacies fit for the throne went first to the Court of Sacrifices and the Provisioners, who picked the best and matched flavor to the new offering.
value.literal: If seasonal novelties were fit to present to the sovereign, the responsible office first sent them to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and coordinated with the Imperial Provisioners, selecting the finest and pairing them with flavors suited to the new goods.

value.zh: 太常卿奉薦於太廟，不出神主。
value.en: The Minister of Sacrifices presented at the Great Temple without removing the tablets.
value.literal: The Minister of Imperial Sacrifices presented offerings at the Great Temple without bringing out the spirit tablets.

value.zh: 仲春薦冰，亦如之。
value.en: Mid-spring ice offerings followed the same rule.
value.literal: In mid-spring ice was presented—in the same manner.

value.zh: 文明元年八月，奉高宗神主祔於太廟中，始遷宣皇帝神主于夾室。
value.en: Wenming 1, eighth month: Gaozong's tablet was enshrined in the Grand Temple, and Xuan's tablet was moved to the side chamber for the first time.
value.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Wenming, Gaozong's spirit tablet was enshrined within the Grand Temple; for the first time, Emperor Xuan's spirit tablet was moved to the side chamber.

value.zh: 垂拱四年正月，又於東都立高祖、太宗、高宗三廟，四時享祀，如京廟之儀。
value.en: Chuigong 4, first month: the eastern capital gained temples to Gaozu, Taizong, and Gaozong, with seasonal rites matching the capital.
value.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Chuigong, three temples for Gaozu, Taizong, and Gaozong were also established in the eastern capital; the four seasonal offerings followed the rites of the capital temples.

value.zh: 別立崇先廟以享武氏祖考。
value.en: A separate Chongxian Temple was built for Wu clan ancestors.
value.literal: A separate Chongxian Temple was established to offer to the Wu clan ancestors.

value.zh: 則天尋又令所司議立崇先廟室數，司禮博士、崇文館學士周忭希旨，請立崇先廟為七室，其皇室太廟，減為五室。
value.en: Zetian soon ordered debate on Chongxian's chamber count; Zhou Ping of Spring Rites, courting her wish, urged seven chambers for Chongxian and five for the imperial temple.
value.literal: Empress Zetian soon again ordered the offices to deliberate on how many chambers the Chongxian Temple should have; Court of Spring Rites erudite and Scholar of the Chongwen Institute Zhou Ping, to please her intent, requested seven chambers for Chongxian Temple and reduction of the imperial ancestral temple to five chambers.

value.zh: 春官侍郎賈大隱奏曰：「臣竊准秦、漢皇太后臨朝稱制，並據禮經正文，天子七廟，諸侯五廟。
value.en: Jia Dayin of Spring Rites wrote: "Qin and Han dowagers who ruled from court all cited canon—the Son of Heaven keeps seven temples, lords five.
value.literal: Vice Minister of the Court of Spring Rites Jia Dayin memorialized, saying: "Your subject ventures to cite Qin and Han, when empress dowagers held court and exercised regulatory power—all followed the canonical ritual texts: the Son of Heaven has seven temples, feudal lords five temples.

value.zh: 蓋百王不易之義，萬代常行之法，未有越禮違古而擅裁儀注者也。
value.en: That is the immovable rule of kings and ages—none has broken ritual to rewrite ceremony at will.
value.literal: This is the unchanging meaning of the hundred kings, the constant law of myriad generations—never has anyone transgressed ritual and antiquity to arrogate regulation of ceremony.

value.zh: 今周悰別引浮議，廣述異文，直崇臨朝權儀，不依國家常度，升崇先之廟而七，降國家之廟而五。
value.en: Zhou Cong now cites loose opinion and stray texts, exalting a regent's provisional rite over state norm—seven for Chongxian, five for the realm.
value.literal: Now Zhou Cong cites floating opinions and broadly sets forth heterodox texts, directly elevating provisional rites of holding court, not relying on the state's constant norms—raising Chongxian temple to seven while lowering the state temple to five.

value.zh: 臣聞皇圖廣辟，實崇宗社之尊；
value.en: I have heard: when the throne's design is wide, the altars of state gain honor;
value.literal: Your subject has heard: when the imperial design is broadly opened, it truly honors the altars of state;

value.zh: 帝業弘基，實等山河之固。
value.en: when its foundation is vast, it matches mountains and rivers in firmness.
value.literal: when the imperial enterprise has a vast foundation, it truly equals the solidity of mountains and rivers.

value.zh: 伏以天步多艱，時逢遏密，代天理物，自古有之。
value.en: Heaven's course has been hard; times of mourning seclusion came; regents who govern for Heaven are ancient.
value.literal: Your subject observes: the heavenly steps have been many times arduous; times encountered mourning seclusion; one who substitutes for Heaven and governs things has existed since antiquity.

value.zh: 伏惟皇太后親承顧托，憂勤黎庶，納孝慈之請，垂矜撫之懷，實所謂光顯大猷，恢崇聖載。
value.en: The Dowager took the trust, toiled for the people, heard pleas of filial mercy, and soothed the realm—truly glorifying the great design and widening the sage charge.
value.literal: Your subject respectfully considers: the Empress Dowager personally received the entrustment, labored in care for the common people, accepted the request of filial piety and compassion, extended a cherishing and soothing heart—this truly is what is called to glorify the great plan and expand the sage burden.

value.zh: 其崇先廟室，合同諸侯之數，國家宗廟，不合輒有移變。
value.en: Chongxian should match a lord's count; the state temple must not be casually altered.
value.literal: Chambers of Chongxian Temple should accord with the feudal lord count; the state ancestral temple must not casually be shifted.

value.zh: 臣之愚直，並依正禮，周忭之請，實乖古儀。」
value.en: Your subject's stubborn directness wholly follows orthodox ritual; Zhou Ping's request truly contravenes ancient ceremony."
value.literal: Your subject's stubborn directness wholly follows orthodox ritual; Zhou Ping's request truly contravenes ancient ceremony."

value.zh: 則天由是且止，
value.en: Zetian held off for the moment.
value.literal: Zetian therefore stopped for the time being,

value.zh: 昔黃帝有子二十五人，或內列諸華，或外分荒服，昌意少子，受封北土，國有大鮮卑山，因以為號。
value.en: Long ago the Yellow Emperor had twenty-five sons: some served within the Chinese heartland, others were sent to govern the outer marches. Changyi, his youngest, was enfeoffed in the north, where the great Xianbei Mountain stood—and from that mountain the people took their name.
value.literal: In olden times the Yellow Emperor had twenty-five sons; some were enrolled within the Chinese domains, some were apportioned to distant borderlands. Changyi was his youngest son; he received a fief in the northern lands. The state had the great Xianbei Mountain, and from it took its name.

value.zh: 其後，世為君長，統幽都之北，廣漠之野，畜牧遷徙，射獵為業，淳樸為俗，簡易為化，不為文字，刻木紀契而已，世事遠近，人相傳授，如史官之紀錄焉。
value.en: Afterward they ruled generation upon generation north of Youdu, across the wide steppe. They lived by herding, moving with the seasons, and by the hunt; their ways were plain, their customs unadorned. They had no script—only notches cut in wood to seal bargains. What happened near and far was handed down mouth to mouth, much as if scribes had kept annals.
value.literal: Thereafter generation after generation they were chieftains, ruling north of Youdu in the vast deserts. Pastoral migration and hunting were their livelihood; simplicity their custom, plainness their transformation. They did not use writing, but only carved wood to record agreements. Affairs near and far were passed from person to person, like the records of historians.

value.zh: 黃帝以土德王，北俗謂土為托，謂后為跋，故以為氏。
value.en: The Yellow Emperor reigned under the virtue of Earth; northerners called earth tuo and called a queen ba—so the clan took the name Tuoba.
value.literal: The Yellow Emperor ruled by the virtue of Earth; in northern custom earth was called tuo and a queen was called ba, hence they took it as their clan name.

value.zh: 其裔始均，入仕堯世，逐女魃於弱水之北，民賴其勤，帝舜嘉之，命為田祖。
value.en: A descendant, Shijun, served in the reign of Yao, driving the drought demon Nüba beyond the Weak Water. The people owed their relief to his labor; Shun commended him and named him Lord of the Fields.
value.literal: His descendant Shijun entered service in the age of Yao, drove Nüba north of the Weak Water; the people relied on his diligence, Emperor Shun praised him, and appointed him Lord of the Fields.

value.zh: 爰歷三代，以及秦漢，獯鬻、獫狁、山戎、匈奴之屬，累代殘暴，作害中州，而始均之裔，不交南夏，是以載籍無聞焉。
value.en: Through the Three Dynasties and on into Qin and Han, the Xiongnu and their kindred peoples—Xunyu, Xianyun, Shanrong—ravaged the Central Plains generation after generation. Yet Shijun's line never dealt with the southern realms, and so the written histories say nothing of them.
value.literal: Thus through the Three Dynasties down to Qin and Han, the Xunyu, Xianyun, Shanrong, Xiongnu and their kind were generation after generation violent, harming the Central States—but the descendants of Shijun did not mingle with Southern Xia, and therefore they go unmentioned in written records.

value.zh: 二十八年春正月，衞辰謀反，東渡河。
value.en: In the first month of spring of the twenty-eighth year Weichen plotted rebellion and crossed the river to the east.
value.literal: In the first month of spring of the twenty-eighth year Weichen plotted rebellion and crossed the river eastward.

value.zh: 帝討之，衞辰懼而遁走。
value.en: The emperor attacked him, and Weichen fled in fear.
value.literal: The emperor attacked him; Weichen, in fear, fled.

value.zh: 冬十二月，苻堅遣使朝貢。
value.en: In the twelfth month of winter Fu Jian sent envoys with tribute.
value.literal: In the twelfth month of winter Fu Jian sent envoys with tribute.

value.zh: 是歲，司馬千齡死，弟弈僭立。
value.en: That year Sima Qianling died, and his younger brother Yi usurped the throne.
value.literal: That year Sima Qianling died; his younger brother Yi usurped the throne.

value.zh: 三十四年春，長孫斤謀反，伏誅。
value.en: In the spring of the thirty-fourth year Changsun Jin plotted rebellion and was executed.
value.literal: In the spring of the thirty-fourth year Changsun Jin plotted rebellion and was executed.

value.zh: 斤之反也，拔刃向御座，太子獻明皇帝諱寔格之，傷脅。
value.en: When Jin rebelled he drew his blade toward the throne; the crown prince—the future Emperor Xianming, taboo name Shi—blocked him and was wounded in the flank.
value.literal: When Jin rebelled he drew his blade toward the imperial seat; the crown prince, the future Emperor Xianming, taboo name Shi, blocked him and was wounded in the flank.

value.zh: 夏五月，薨，後追諡焉。
value.en: In the fifth month of summer he died; a posthumous title was conferred later.
value.literal: In the fifth month of summer he died; posthumous title was conferred afterward.

value.zh: 秋七月，皇孫珪生，大赦。
value.en: In the seventh month of autumn the imperial grandson Gui was born, and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
value.literal: In the seventh month of autumn the imperial grandson Gui was born; a general amnesty was proclaimed.

value.zh: 是年，司馬弈臣桓溫，廢弈為海西公，立叡子昱。
value.en: That year Sima Yi's subject Huan Wen deposed Yi as Prince of Haixi and enthroned Rui's son Yu.
value.literal: That year the minister Sima Yi's subject Huan Wen deposed Yi as Prince of Haixi and installed Rui's son Yu.

value.zh: 司馬休之 司馬楚之 司馬景之 司馬叔璠 司馬天助
value.en: Sima Xiuzhi, Sima Chuzhi, Sima Jingzhi, Sima Shufan, and Sima Tianzhu
value.literal: Sima Xiuzhi, Sima Chuzhi, Sima Jingzhi, Sima Shufan, Sima Tianzhu

value.zh: 子裔，字承業。
value.en: His son Yi, whose courtesy name was Chengye.
value.literal: His son Yi, styled Chengye.

value.zh: 世宗時，悅等為裔理嫡，還襲祖爵。
value.en: Under Emperor Xuanwu (Shizong), Yue and others upheld Yi's claim as legitimate heir, and he recovered the ancestral title.
value.literal: During Shizong's time, Yue and others argued Yi's case as legitimate heir, and he returned to inherit the ancestral title.

value.zh: 位至後軍將軍。
value.en: He rose to General of the Rear Guard.
value.literal: He reached the post of General of the Rear Guard.

value.zh: 卒，贈征虜將軍、洛州刺史。
value.en: He died and was posthumously made General Who Captures Barbarians and Inspector of Luo.
value.literal: He died and was posthumously awarded General Who Captures Barbarians and Inspector of Luo province.

value.zh: 子藏，襲。
value.en: His son Zang inherited the title.
value.literal: His son Zang inherited.

value.zh: 齊受禪，例降。
value.en: When Qi took the throne, his rank was reduced in the usual way.
value.literal: When Qi received the mandate, by precedent his rank was reduced.

value.zh: 異域上
value.en: Other Regions, Part One
value.literal: Other Regions, Part One

value.zh: 天和元年，詔開府陸騰督王亮、司馬裔等討之。
value.en: In the first year of  Lu Teng was ordered to command Wang Liang, Sima Yi, and others against them.
value.literal: In the first year of Tianhe, an edict ordered Opening Office Lu Teng to supervise Wang Liang, Sima Yi, and others in the campaign.

value.zh: 騰水陸俱進，次于湯口，先遣喻之。
value.en: Lu Teng advanced by land and water to Tangkou and first sent envoys to warn them.
value.literal: Teng advanced by land and water together and halted at Tangkou, first sending envoys to admonish them.

value.zh: 而令賢方增浚城池，嚴設扞禦。
value.en: Meanwhile Lingxian deepened walls and strengthened defenses.
value.literal: Meanwhile Lingxian was deepening moats and walls and setting stern defenses.

value.zh: 遣其長子西黎、次子南王領其支屬，於江南險要之地置立十城，遠結涔陽蠻為其聲援。
value.en: He sent sons Xili and the Southern King to ten strongpoints in the south, allying with the Cenyang Man.
value.literal: He sent his eldest son Xili and second son the Southern King with their dependents to ten fortified places on the Jiang south's strategic heights, linking far with the Cenyang Man as their support.

value.zh: 令賢率其精卒，固守水邏城。
value.en: Lingxian held Shuilo with his elite troops.
value.literal: Lingxian himself led his picked troops and held fast at Shuilo Fortress.

value.zh: 騰乃總集將帥，謀其進趣。
value.en: Lu Teng gathered his officers to plan the advance.
value.literal: Teng then gathered the generals to plan the advance.

value.zh: 咸欲先取水邏，然後經畧江南。
value.en: All favored taking Shuilo first, then the south bank.
value.literal: All wished first to take Shuilo and then deal with the Jiang south.

value.zh: 騰言於衆曰：「令賢內恃水邏金湯之險，外托涔陽輔車之援，兼復資糧充實，器械精新。
value.en: Lu Teng told them: "Lingxian trusts Shuilo's defenses and Cenyang's aid, with full stores and fresh arms.
value.literal: Teng said to the assembly: "Lingxian relies within on Shuilo's golden moat and without on Cenyang's chariot-pole support, and moreover his provisions are full and weapons new and fine.

value.zh: 以我懸軍攻其嚴壘，脫一戰不剋，更成其氣。
value.en: If our isolated force assaults his fortress and fails once, his morale will rise.
value.literal: If we as a suspended army attack his strong fortress and by chance one battle fails, his spirit will only grow.

value.zh: 不如頓軍湯口，先取江南，剪其羽毛，然後進軍水邏。
value.en: Better to hold at Tangkou, take the south bank first, clip his wings, then strike Shuilo.
value.literal: Better to halt the army at Tangkou, first take the Jiang south, cut his feathers, and then advance on Shuilo.

value.zh: 此制勝之計也。」
value.en: That is how we win."
value.literal: This is the plan for certain victory."

value.zh: 衆皆然之。
value.en: All agreed.
value.literal: The multitude all approved.

value.zh: 乃遣開府王亮率衆渡江，旬日攻拔其八城，凶黨奔散。
value.en: Wang Liang crossed the river and in ten days took eight forts; the rebels fled.
value.literal: He then sent Opening Office Wang Liang with troops across the river; in ten days they stormed eight fortresses and the rebels scattered.

value.zh: 獲賊帥冉承公幷生口三千人，降其部衆一千戶。
value.en: They took Ran Chenggong and three thousand captives and accepted a thousand households in surrender.
value.literal: They captured the bandit leader Ran Chenggong together with three thousand captives and received the submission of a thousand households.

value.zh: 遂簡募驍勇，數道入攻水邏。
value.en: They then picked elite troops and assaulted Shuilo on several routes.
value.literal: Then they selected fierce warriors and attacked Shuilo by several routes.

value.zh: 路經石壁城。
value.en: The march passed Shibi Fortress.
value.literal: The route passed Shibi Fortress.

value.zh: 此城峻嶮，四面壁立，故以名焉。
value.en: The fortress was sheer, walled on every side, hence its name.
value.literal: This fortress was steep and perilous, with walls standing on all four sides—hence the name.

value.zh: 唯有一小路，緣梯而上。
value.en: Only one path climbed by ladder.
value.literal: There was only one narrow path, climbing by ladder.

value.zh: 蠻蜑以為峭絕，非兵衆所行。
value.en: The Man thought it impassable for an army.
value.literal: The Man and boat peoples thought it too sheer for troops to pass.

value.zh: 騰被甲先登，衆軍繼進，備經危阻，累月乃得舊路。
value.en: Lu Teng armored himself and led the climb; the army followed through months of peril.
value.literal: Teng donned armor and climbed first; the army followed, enduring repeated dangers, and only after months regained the old route.

value.zh: 且騰先任隆州總管，雅知蠻帥冉伯犁、冉安西與令賢有隙。
value.en: Lu Teng, former Longzhou commander, knew the Man chiefs Ran Boli and Ran Anxi hated Lingxian.
value.literal: Moreover Teng had earlier served as Commander of Long Prefecture and knew well that the Man leaders Ran Boli and Ran Anxi were at odds with Lingxian.

value.zh: 騰乃招誘伯犁等，結為父子，又多遺其金帛。
value.en: He won over Boli with gifts and sworn brotherhood.
value.literal: Teng then enticed Boli and others, binding them as sworn kin, and also sent them much gold and silk.

value.zh: 伯犁等悅，遂為鄉導。
value.en: Boli gladly guided the army.
value.literal: Boli and the others were pleased and then served as local guides.

value.zh: 水邏側又有石勝城者，亦是險要。
value.en: Near Shuilo stood Shisheng Fortress, also a strongpoint.
value.literal: Beside Shuilo there was also Shisheng Fortress, likewise strategic.

value.zh: 令賢使兄子龍真據之。
value.en: Lingxian put his nephew Long Zhen there.
value.literal: Lingxian sent his elder brother's son Long Zhen to hold it.

value.zh: 騰又密誘龍真云，若平水邏，使其代令賢處。
value.en: Lu Teng secretly promised Long Zhen Lingxian's place if Shuilo fell.
value.literal: Teng also secretly enticed Long Zhen, saying that if Shuilo were pacified he would place him in Lingxian's seat.

value.zh: 龍真大悅，密遣其子詣騰。
value.en: Long Zhen sent his son to Lu Teng in secret.
value.literal: Long Zhen was greatly pleased and secretly sent his son to Teng.

value.zh: 騰乃厚加禮接，賜以金帛。
value.en: Lu Teng received him with honor and gifts of gold and silk.
value.literal: Teng then treated him with generous courtesy and bestowed gold and silk.

value.zh: 蠻貪利旣深，仍請立效。
value.en: Greedy for the bounty, the Man asked to prove their loyalty in battle.
value.literal: The Man, their greed for profit now deep, still asked to pledge achievement.

value.zh: 乃謂騰曰：「欲翻所據城，恐人力寡少。」
value.en: He told Lu Teng: "I want to turn the fortress I hold, but I lack men."
value.literal: He then said to Teng: "I wish to turn the fortress I hold, but fear my manpower is too few."

value.zh: 騰許以三百兵助之。
value.en: Lu Teng promised three hundred men to help.
value.literal: Teng promised three hundred troops to assist him.

value.zh: 旣而遣二千人銜枚夜進。
value.en: Then he sent two thousand men with gags in their mouths by night.
value.literal: Presently he sent two thousand men with gags in their mouths advancing by night.

value.zh: 龍真力不能禦，遂平石勝城。
value.en: Long Zhen could not hold out and Shisheng fell.
value.literal: Long Zhen's strength could not resist, and Shisheng Fortress was pacified.

value.zh: 晨至水邏，蠻衆大潰，斬首萬餘級，虜獲一萬口。
value.en: By dawn they reached Shuilo; the Man army collapsed with more than ten thousand killed and ten thousand taken.
value.literal: At dawn they reached Shuilo; the Man masses broke in great rout, more than ten thousand heads cut off and ten thousand mouths captured.

value.zh: 令賢遁走，追而獲之，幷其子弟等皆斬之。
value.en: Lingxian fled, was caught, and was executed with his sons and kin.
value.literal: Lingxian fled; pursued and captured, together with his sons and younger kin all were beheaded.

value.zh: 司馬裔又別下其二十餘城，獲蠻帥冉三公等。
value.en: Sima Yi took twenty-odd cities and captured the Man chief Ran Sangong.
value.literal: Sima Yi separately reduced more than twenty of their cities and captured the Man leader Ran Sangong and others.

value.zh: 騰乃積其骸骨於水邏城側，為京觀。
value.en: Lu Teng piled their bones beside Shuilo as a victory mound.
value.literal: Teng then heaped their bones beside Shuilo Fortress as a skull mound.

value.zh: 後蠻蜑望見，輒大號哭。
value.en: When the Man saw the mound they wailed aloud.
value.literal: Later when the Man and boat peoples saw it, they would wail loudly.

value.zh: 自此狼戾之心輟矣。
value.en: After that their fierce spirit broke.
value.literal: From this their fierce hearts were stilled.

value.zh: 時向五子王據石默城，令其子寶勝據雙城。
value.en: Xiang the Fifth Son King held Shimo and sent his son Baosheng to hold Shuang.
value.literal: At that time Xiang the Fifth Son King held Shimo Fortress and ordered his son Baosheng to hold Shuang Fortress.

value.zh: 水邏平後，頻遣喻之，而五子王猶不從命。
value.en: After Shuilo fell Lu Teng warned them repeatedly, but the Fifth Son King refused.
value.literal: After Shuilo was pacified he repeatedly sent envoys to admonish them, yet the Fifth Son King still did not obey.

value.zh: 騰又遣王亮屯牢坪，司馬裔屯雙城以圖之。
value.en: Lu Teng sent Wang Liang to Laoping and Sima Yi to Shuang to besiege them.
value.literal: Teng again sent Wang Liang to encamp at Laoping and Sima Yi to encamp at Shuang to besiege them.

value.zh: 騰慮雙城孤峭，攻未易拔。
value.en: He feared Shuang was too steep to storm easily.
value.literal: Teng worried that Shuang was isolated and steep and would not be easy to storm.

value.zh: 賊若委城奔散，又難追討。
value.en: If the rebels fled the city they would be hard to catch.
value.literal: If the bandits abandoned the city and scattered, pursuit would again be hard.

value.zh: 乃令諸軍周回立柵，遏其走路。
value.en: He ringed the forts with palisades to block escape.
value.literal: He then ordered the armies to encircle with palisades on all sides, blocking their escape routes.

value.zh: 賊乃大駭。
value.en: The rebels panicked.
value.literal: The bandits were greatly terrified.

value.zh: 於是縱兵擊破之，擒五子王于石默，獲寶勝於雙城，悉斬諸向首領，生擒萬餘口。
value.en: His troops broke them, took the Fifth Son King at Shimo and Baosheng at Shuang, executed the Xiang chiefs, and captured ten thousand alive.
value.literal: Thereupon he unleashed the troops to break them; the Fifth Son King was seized at Shimo and Baosheng captured at Shuang; all the Xiang chiefs were beheaded and more than ten thousand taken alive.

value.zh: 信州舊治白帝。
value.en: Xin Prefecture had formerly been at Baidi.
value.literal: Xin Prefecture's old seat was Baidi.

value.zh: 騰更于劉備故宮城南，八陣之北，臨江岸築城，移置信州。
value.en: Lu Teng built a new city south of Liu Bei's old palace and north of the Eight Formations and moved Xin Prefecture there.
value.literal: Teng then south of the former palace of Liu Bei and north of the Eight Formations, on the river bank built a city and moved Xin Prefecture there.

value.zh: 又以巫縣、信陵、秭歸竝是硤中要險，於是築城置防，以為襟帶焉。
value.en: He fortified Wu, Xinling, and Zigui in the gorges as strategic strongpoints.
value.literal: He also took Wu, Xinling, and Zigui—all strategic points in the gorges—and built cities and defenses as strategic belts.

value.zh: 資治通鑑 第169卷卷第一百六十九
value.en: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 169.
value.literal: Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Governance, Volume 169, the one hundred sixty-ninth fascicle.

value.zh: 臣光曰：夫臣之事君，宜將順其美，正救其惡。
value.en: Sima Guang comments: A minister serving his sovereign should nurture what is good in him and correct what is evil.
value.literal: Chen Guang remarks: In a subject's service to his ruler, he ought to nurture and follow the ruler's virtues and straightly remedy his faults.

value.zh: 孔奐在陳，處腹心之重任，決禮義之大計，苟以世祖之言為不誠，則當如竇嬰面辯，袁盎廷爭，防微杜漸以絕覬覦之心。
value.en: Kong Huan in Chen occupied a position of deepest trust and weighed the gravest questions of ritual and right. If he believed Emperor Wendi's intent was false, he should have remonstrated as Dou Ying did in open debate, or as Yuan Ang did at court—stopping the rot early and cutting off all who would plot usurpation.
value.literal: Kong Huan in Chen held a trusted post at the ruler's heart and decided great questions of ritual and righteousness; if he took Shizu's words as insincere, then he ought, like Dou Ying, to argue face to face, or like Yuan Ang, to contend in court—to stop evil at the sprout and cut off covetous designs.

value.zh: 以為誠邪，則當請明下詔書，宣告中外，使世祖有宋宣之美，高宗無楚靈之惡。
value.en: If he took the emperor at his word, he should have asked for a clear edict proclaimed at home and abroad, so that Wendi would gain the praise owed Duke Xuan of Song and the court would not repeat the evil of King Ling of Chu.
value.literal: If he thought them sincere, then he ought to request a clear proclamation, announcing it within and without, so that Shizu might have the beauty of Duke Xuan of Song, and Gaozong would lack the evil of King Ling of Chu.

value.zh: 不然，謂太子嫡嗣，不可動搖，欲保附而安全之，則當盡忠竭節，以死繼之，如晉之荀息，趙之肥義。
value.en: Or, if he held the heir's position inviolable and wished only to cling to power in safety, he should have given his utmost loyalty unto death, as Xun Xi of Jin or Fei Yi of Zhao did.
value.literal: Otherwise, holding that the crown prince as legitimate heir could not be shaken, wishing to preserve and attach himself and win safety, then he ought to exhaust loyalty and drain his integrity, following in death, like Xun Xi of Jin or Fei Yi of Zhao.

value.zh: 奈何於君之存，則逆探其情而求合焉；
value.en: Yet while the emperor still lived, he probed obliquely for the ruler's hidden wishes and strove to conform to them.
value.literal: Yet how was it that while the ruler still lived, he inversely probed his feelings to seek accord?

value.zh: 及其既沒，則權臣移國而不能救，嗣主失位而不能死！
value.en: When the emperor was gone, powerful ministers seized the state and he could not save it; the rightful heir was dethroned and he would not die in his defense!
value.literal: When he had already died, powerful ministers shifted the realm yet he could not rescue it; the heir lost his place yet he could not die for it!

value.zh: 斯乃奸諛之尤者，而世祖謂之遺直，以托六尺之孤，豈不悖哉！
value.en: Here was flattery at its worst—yet Emperor Wendi called him a minister straight as those of old and entrusted to him his young son: how perverse!
value.literal: This is the extreme of flattery and deceit—yet Shizu called him a straight remnant of antiquity and entrusted to him a six-foot orphan: is this not perverse!

value.zh: 癸酉，上殂。
value.en: On the day guiyou, the emperor died.
value.literal: On guiyou, the emperor died.

value.zh: 周信州蠻冉令賢、向五子王等據巴峽反，攻陷白帝，黨與連結二千餘里。
value.en: In Zhou's Xinzhou, the chieftains Ran Lingxian and Xiang Wuzi Wang seized the Ba Gorge and rebelled, capturing Baidi; their allies stretched along more than two thousand li.
value.literal: Zhou's Xinzhou barbarians Ran Lingxian, Xiang Wuzi Wang, and others held the Ba Gorge and rebelled, storming and taking Baidi; their partisans linked for more than two thousand li.

value.zh: 周遣開府儀同三司元契、趙剛等前後討之，終不克。
value.en: Zhou dispatched Yuan Qi, Zhao Gang, and other commissioners of equal protocol in successive campaigns, but could not subdue them.
value.literal: Zhou sent commissioners with equal protocol Yuan Qi, Zhao Gang, and others, in successive campaigns to attack them, but in the end could not overcome them.

value.zh: 九月，詔開府儀同三司陸騰督開府儀同三司王亮、司馬裔討之。
value.en: In the ninth month, an edict put Commissioner Lu Teng in overall command of Wang Liang and Sima Yi to suppress the rebels.
value.literal: In the ninth month, an edict ordered Commissioner Lu Teng to supervise Commissioners Wang Liang and Sima Yi in attacking them.

value.zh: 信州舊治白帝，騰徙之於八陳灘北，以司馬裔為信州刺史。
value.en: Teng moved the Xinzhou seat from Baidi to north of the Eight Formations Shoals and appointed Sima Yi governor.
value.literal: Xinzhou's old seat was at Baidi; Teng moved it north of Bachan Beach and made Sima Yi Governor of Xinzhou.
